sentences.text:
1. The present acquittal Appeal has been filed by the R/CR.A/431/2006 JUDGMENT appellant - original complainant under Section 378(4) of Cr. P.C., against the Judgment and order dated 25.2.2002, rendered in P.F.A. Case No.54 of 1996 by the learned Judicial Magistrate First Class,
Surat.
The said case was registered against the present respondents - original accused for the offence under sections 7(i) and 16 of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act (for short "PFA Act").
The said Judgment of the trial Court has been challenged by the appellant on the ground that the Judgment and order passed by learned trial Court is against the law and evidence on record.

2. According to the prosecution case, on 13.7.1995, at about 12:45 p.m., the appellant - Food Inspector visited the respondent No.1 firm and at that time, accused No.3 was present and from him, the appellant purchased 600 gram ground nut oil after opening the sealed tin of 15 Kgs. of company Gopal Brand in the presence of panch and amount of Rs.26.40 was paid to the accused No.3.
Then after dividing the sample into three glass bottles and one was sent to Public Analyst as per the provisions of the Act.
The said sample was found to be adulterated as per the analyst report.
Thereafter, sanction was obtained and complaint was file against the accused.
Therefore, aforesaid Criminal Case was registered.

3. At the conclusion of trial and after appreciating the oral R/CR.A/431/2006 JUDGMENT as well as documentary evidence, the learned trial Judge vide impugned Judgment, acquitted the respondent - accused.
4. Learned advocate Mr. Shah, appearing on behalf of the appellant has contended that the Judgment and order of acquittal is contrary to law and evidence on record and is not proper.
He has contended that learned trial Judge has committed error in acquitting the accused on the ground that there is inconsistency in the deposition of the complainant.

He has further contended that there was proof about licence of supply department and xerox of partnership deed at Exhibit 88 and 89,
whereby it is proved that the accused No.1 is partnership firm and accused Nos. 3 and 4 are partners of the said firm.
He has contended that the trial Court has failed to appreciate the report of Public Analyst.
He has also contended that the offences punishable under the Act are directly connected with the health of public at large.

5. Learned advocate Mr. Modi for the respondent - accused supported the impugned judgment and order of acquittal and he submitted that learned trial Judge has rightly appreciated the evidence produced on record and therefore, no interference is required to be called for.
He lastly submitted that present appeal may kindly be dismissed by confirming the impugned judgment and order of acquittal.

Learned advocate R/CR.A/431/2006 JUDGMENT also cited the decisions of this Court passed in Criminal Appeal Nos.1686 of 2010, 500 of 1996, Criminal Misc. Application No.13589 of 2009 in Criminal Appeal No.2420 of 2009 and decision reported in 2009(1) Crimes 1 (Guj.).

sentences.text:
Heard learned APP Mrs. Hansa Punani for the respondent No.9.
7.
I have gone through the papers produced in the case.
I have also gone through the evidence led before the trial Court as well as the Expert Opinion.
I have also gone through the Judgment of the trial Court.

The learned Magistrate has rightly observed that sanction is not proper and there is no compliance of the Section 10(7) of the Act, as the panch of the complainant has not supported the case of the complainant.
Even there is no document which proved the case that the accused No.1 is a firm and other accused are partners of the said firm.
Learned counsel for the appellant is unable to convince this court as to whether the prosecution has followed the mandatory provision of Rules.
In the facts of the case I am in complete agreement with the reasons assigned by the trial Court.
In view of this position, I am of the view that present case is covered up by the decisions cited by the learned advocate Mr. Modi for the respondents.
Hence, the appeal is required to be dismissed.
R/CR.A/431/2006 JUDGMENT 8.

In the result, the Criminal Appeal is dismissed and order dated 25.2.2002 passed by the learned Judicial Magistrate First Class, Municipal Court, Surat, in P.F.A. Case No.54 of 1996 is hereby confirmed.
